Kinetix 5100 Servo Drive Parameters
For more information see:

column10: Comments

Data Type
Determines the data type of position, speed, acceleration reference, feedback and all related values.
0 = DINT

Position Data Unit
Determines the data unit of position reference and feedback and all related attributes.
0 = PUU

Speed Data Unit
Determines the data unit of speed reference and feedback and all related attributes.
1 = 0.1RPM

Acceleration Data Unit
Determines the data unit of acceleration (deceleration) reference and feedback and all related attributes.
1 = 0.1RPM/s

Torque Data Unit
Determines the data unit of torque reference and feedback and all related attributes.
1 = 0.1%

Torque Ramp Time Unit
Determines the data unit of torque slope.
0 = millisecond

Operating Mode
Determines the drive operating mode when ID25 (Start Motion) has a zero-to-one transition.
0 = Mode not specified
1 = Position mode
2 = Speed mode
3 = Home mode
4 = Torque mode
5 = Gear mode
6 = Index mode

Servo On
A zero-to-one transition will activate the drive.

Servo Off
A zero-to-one transition will de-activate the drive.

Stop Motion
A zero-to-one transition will stop the drive.

Fault Reset
A zero-to-one transition will try to clear a fault on the drive.

Start Motion
A zero-to-one transition means the motion command has been issued from the external controller.
Speed Reference

Acceleration Reference
Determines the command speed, and its range is based on Speed Data Unit.

Deceleration Reference
Determines the command acceleration, and its range is based on Acceleration Data Unit.
Homing MethodDefines the homing method.See ID 29 (Homing Method) on Detailed Definitions tab

Position Reference
Determines the command position, and its range is based on Position Data Unit.

Home Return Speed
Determines the command creep speed, and its range is based on Speed Data Unit.

Non-Cyclic Move Type
Defines the position command selection.
0 = absolute positioning
1 = relative positioning
2 = incremental positioning
3 = high-speed position capturing

Torque Reference
Determines the command torque, and its range is based on Torque Data Unit.

Torque RampTime
Determines the command torque slope, and its range is based on Torque Slope Unit.

Position Command Overlap
Determines whether overlapping of the next movement is allowed.
0 = Overlap of next movement is not allowed
1 = Overlap of next movement is allowed

Position Command Override
Determines whether this movement can interrupt previous movement.
0 = Interrupt is not allowed
1 = Interrupt is allowed

Travel Mode
Selects the move type.
2 = Non-Cyclic Move Type
10 = Cyclic Move Type

Cyclic MoveType
Determines the direction of movement.
0 = Rotary Positive
1 = Rotary Negative
2 = Rotary shortest path

Captured Position Select
Selects the first capture or the second capture.
0 = First capture (trigger by DI9)
1 = Second capture (trigger by DI10)

Starting Index
Defines the first index that the drive should execute.

Network mode
0 = local input
1 = network

Operating Mode State
Indicates which operating mode the drive remains in.
0 = mode not specified
1 = Position mode
2 = Speed mode
3 = Home mode
4 = Torque mode
5 = Gear mode
6 = Index mode

At Reference
Drive whether the drive is at actual reference (position, speed, torque) based on mode.
0=Drive not actual at reference (position, speed, torque) based on mode
1=Drive actual at reference (position, speed, torque) based on mode

Ready
0=Drive is not ready
1=Drive is ready

Active
Indicates whether the drive is ready for a servo on action.
0 – Drive has not has successfully received the Servo On command
1 – Drive has successfully received the Servo On command

Warning Present
Indicates whether the drive is in a warning state.
0=Drive is not in warning state
1=Drive is in warning state

Fault
Indicates whether the drive is in a faulted state.
0=Drive is not in faulted state
1=Drive is in faulted state

Stopped
Indicates whether the drive is stopped.
0=Drive is not stopped
1=Drive is stopped

Fault Code
Displays the fault code.
See View Status and Faults in the user manual.

0=Reserved
1=Over current
2=Over voltage
3=Under voltage

Warning Code
Displays warning code.
See View Status and Faults in the user manual.

0…12 Reserved
13=Emergency Stop
14=Reverse Limit Error
15=Forward Limit Error

Actual Position
Indicates the actual position of the drive.

Actual Speed
Indicates the actual speed of the drive.

Actual Torque
Indicates the actual torque of the drive.

Active Index
Indicates the currently executing index.

Homed Status
Indicates whether the home action is completed.
0=Home is not completed
1=Home is completed

Command In Progress
Indicates whether the motion command is in progress.
0=No motion command is in progress
1=Motion command is in progress

Motor Category
Defines the type of motor connected to the drive.
0=No motor connected
1=Rotary motor connected
2=Linear motor connected

Uncertain
indicates whether the data may be inaccurate
0=no question about data validity
1=data validity is questionable

Sets the master position reference
0 - Reserved
1 – Auxiliary encoder
2 – Pulse Command (I/O terminal)
3 – Reserved
4 – Virtual Pulse from Timeline (1K Hz)

Sets CAM stop mode
0 – stop immediately
1 – decelerate and stop

Selects the method used to execute the cam profile.
0 = Immediate – The slave axis is immediately locked to the master axis and the position camming process begins.
1 = Reserved
2 = Forward only – the cam profile starts when the master position crosses the Master Lock Position in the forward direction.
3 = Reverse only – the cam profile starts when the master position crosses the Master Lock Position in the reverse direction.
4 = Shorteset Path – the cam profile starts when the master position crosses the Master Lock Position in the shortest path.

Determines if the cam profile is executed only one time or repeatedly:
0 = Once – cam motion of slave axis is executed one time according to the value of CamMasterUnlockCounts, and then the Process Complete bit is set.
1 = Continuous – Once started the cam profile is executed indefinitely. This feature is useful in rotary applications where it is necessary that the cam position run continuously in a rotary or reciprocating fashion.
